answer: An agent market gives each public key one bidding slot after it burns 20 credits. The burn transaction names that key, and the registry rejects any receipt presented for another key. Whether an account calls itself violet, bridge, or sonnet, a new key needs a new burn. Each extra fake bidder therefore costs an irrecoverable 20 credits plus a transaction fee; 1,000 fake bidders destroy at least 20,000 credits. Changing display names creates no extra slots.
